content:
Kia Central & South America has become an official sponsor of the LCS and CBLOL, two of the most important League of Legends leagues in the Americas

The partnership strengthens the brands connection with an industry that brings together more than 300 million players across Latin America

title: Faker targets second Asian Games gold with Korea esports team
summary: Faker targets second Asian Games gold with Korea esports team  Korea JoongAng Daily
content:
Korea's 44-member esports team is aiming for five gold medals in Japan, with Faker returning for League of Legends.

The Korean national team for the esports category in the upcoming Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games held a kickoff ceremony Tuesday and shared their ambitions.

After debuting as a demonstration sport at the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta, esports will be held as an official medal sport for the second time at the quadrennial event, set to kick off Sept. 19 in Japan this year.

Korea will send a team of 44 people, including 36 athletes, to compete in nine of 11 esports genres. The number of athletes and competing events has more than doubled from the 2022 Asian Games held in Hangzhou, China, the Korea esports Association said.

The esports star Lee Sang-hyeok, best known as Faker, will be vying for a second gold medal in League of Legends (LoL) as part of the national team this year.

"Since the Korean people have high hopes for the esports category, I want to fulfill that hope [...] and give them back pride and honor," Faker said at a press conference in Seoul, adding that he feels more excited than stressed ahead of the competition.

title: Spanish grassroots LoL event under fire due to racist team name and comments
summary: Spanish grassroots LoL event under fire due to racist team name and comments  Esports News UK
content:
Update 16:20 BST: The local region organisers in Spain,Circuito Tormenta, have banned the team and players on the Klan till 2027. Furthermore, the JetaCup as lost all support systems and tools with the company revoking its licence to operate officially in Spanish LoL.

A community-created League of Legends tournament, the JetaCup, has come under fire after after promotional material for one of its participating teams appeared to reference the Ku Klux Klan. The drama escalated further with what appear to be now-deleted tweets on X. Screenshots circulated alongside also appear to show racial jokes involving Lucian and Senna, two non-white League of Legends champions.

The event features a team called KeKe Clan, whose name and promotional imagery have been interpreted by critics as references to the KKK, the American white supremacist group. The organisation has a long history of racial terror and violence against Black Americans, including lynchings. Screenshots of the deleted tweets have since been archived via aReddit thread, attributed to at least one person associated with the team, showing additional posts that commenters have linked to the same controversy.

The problem is compounded by the event’s associations. The tournament carries the name of renowned Spanish creator, Lyon Toad, giving it additional visibility in the Spanish League of Legends scene.

Last week, the event featured a matchup between SK Gaming’s Head Coach, David “OWN3R” Rodriguez de la Torre, alongside former Heretics coach Victor “Machuki” Machuca Segura. This shows that, despite its grassroots status, the tournament has attracted personnel with considerable experience at the higher echelons of competitive play.
